headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt-injection, leakage, and write-conflict pathways plausible by default; compliance risk is lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes ForwardAuth and OAuth/OIDC flows, while transformers can read/write files, run browsers, and execute subprocesses. A plausible bridge exists if Authelia outputs are fed into transformers via shared files or HTTP responses, but no direct shared channel is documented. Uncertainty keeps this above low.
conditions: IF Authelia outputs are copied into a file or request body that transformers parses as instructions
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or pipeline
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Strip instructions from Authelia-generated content before passing it onward
Add a fixed schema validator before transformers consumes Authelia output
Disable any automatic file-watching bridge between them
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and handles authentication flows; transformers can read the filesystem and send data to the Hugging Face Hub or serve endpoints. If they share a workspace, files touched by Authelia can be read and uploaded by transformers, creating a realistic leakage path. The pairwise interaction is inferred from docs, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents mount the same directory or volume
IF transformers is configured to upload or serve content derived from that directory
mitigations: Use separate service accounts and volumes
Remove secrets from any shared directory
Turn off outbound uploads from transformers
Audit mounted paths for credentials before startup
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Transformers can write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and install packages; Authelia has broad network egress and may participate in shared auth/config workflows. If both operate on the same mutable workspace, concurrent writes can corrupt files or state. Because no locking or isolation is documented, uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git checkout
IF no external lock or orchestrator serializes their mutations
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize write access with a lock file
Run one agent read-only
Snapshot the workspace before each run
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit auth-related outputs that transformers may ingest through files or pipeline APIs. Transformers is capable of downstream actions via subprocesses and shell execution, so an unverified Authelia output could be amplified into incorrect processing or actions. The profiles do not show a mandatory verification step, so the cascade is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF transformers consumes Authelia output as authoritative input
IF downstream scripts or pipelines act on that output without validation
mitigations: Insert a human review step before actioning outputs
Validate Authelia-derived fields against a schema
Log and diff all transformed outputs
Disable automatic execution of generated commands
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication component and transformers processes multimodal content, but neither profile declares regulated data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies. A compliance issue would arise only if sensitive identity data is routed through transformers' broader I/O surfaces. With no explicit mismatch documented, this remains low.
conditions: IF regulated identity data is passed from Authelia into transformers
IF transformers logs or retains that data beyond policy
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Minimize logged fields
Set short retention on intermediate artifacts
Review deployment region and vendor terms
requires-engineering: document data-flow and retention controls
